I'm 60 this year, and I've been farming these 8 mu in Dongfu village, Quzhou County, since I was a teenager. My son works in a factory over in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly me and my wife on the land, though he comes back for the wheat harvest and maize planting rush. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and I listen when the extension agent comes by, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than anything written on paper.

This year I'm sticking with the winter wheat–summer maize double crop on all 8 mu. I did think about cotton last autumn when the price talk was good, but cotton needs too much hand-picking labor and my back isn't what it used to be. Wheat and maize are my insurance: even if one price drops, the other usually holds, and I can always keep wheat in the bin for our own flour if the market turns bad.

For the wheat, I'll sow an improved variety — probably Jimai 22 or whatever certified seed the shop has in stock come October. I stopped saving my own seed three years ago after smut cut my yield by nearly 100 kg per mu. I'll rotary-till the fields before planting. The extension fellow keeps saying 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is plenty, but two seasons back I dropped to 14 kg and the crop went yellow at jointing; my neighbor Lao Wang held steady at 18 kg and out-yielded me by a good 80 kg per mu. So this year I'm putting down about 18 kg N per mu — roughly 100 jin of compound as a base, plus urea topdress at green-up if the plants look thin — and about 6 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium because this soil has been worked hard for forty years. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter if the autumn is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The electricity bill for pumping stings, but missing that last irrigation can cost you 200 kg per mu easy. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and add a fungicide if I see any rust, so three pesticide applications in total. If the weather plays fair, I expect around 480 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, I'll plant hybrid Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605 — same as the rest of the village — right after the wheat comes off the field in early June. The turnaround is only five or six days, so I'll hire the custom operator with the no-till planter to drill straight into the wheat stubble. Tilling costs time and diesel we don't have. I'll apply about 16 kg N per mu, plus 4 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium. Some of the younger farmers are pushing 20 kg N, but 16 kg has given me a steady 500-plus kg per mu and I'd rather not waste money on fertilizer that just runs off. I'll irrigate twice if the summer rains are poor — usually once at the big trumpet stage and again at filling if needed. For pesticides, I'll put down herbicide at sowing and spray for corn borers in July, three applications altogether. I expect about 520 kg per mu from the maize if no big storm flattens it.

It isn't fancy, but it's what I know. I sleep better when I don't gamble.
